findings.title: [P1] Validate stdout-derived paths before opening host files
findings.body: Agent-controlled code can emit `ERROR /dev/zero` alongside a parseable pytest summary. This parser then opens `/dev/zero` on the host and calls an unbounded read, exhausting the grader's memory outside the container and execution timeout. Absolute paths override `tree` in os.path.join; traversal and copied symlinks also escape it. Require paths confined to the grading tree, reject non-regular files, and bound reads. Apply the same checks in def_line().

findings.title: [P1] Avoid following attacker-controlled symlinks during cleanup
findings.body: os.walk includes symlinked directories in ds, and os.chmod follows those links. An agent can replace a grader_protected file with a directory containing a symlink to a host directory. copy_tree preserves the link; prepare() then invokes remove_path() to restore the protected file, changing the external target's permissions to 0700 before container execution. This allows permission changes to directories owned by the grader account and can disrupt shared services or subsequent jobs. Skip symlinks and use directory-relative operations that cannot follow links.

findings.description: The hidden-test grade is purely count based. run_suite/all_pass take `passed`, `total` and the failing node ids from pytest's own output and never check that the overlaid hidden test files (t.overlay dests) were actually collected or passed. The graded tree is the agent's sandbox copy plus the overlay; prepare() only restores paths listed in grader_protected (the seeder lists only infrastructure files that already exist in the fixture). An agent can therefore add a new `pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini` (`python_files = test_mine*.py`, `addopts = --ignore-glob=...`) or a new `conftest.py` (`collect_ignore_glob`, `pytest_collection_modifyitems`, `pytest_runtest_makereport`) and ship N>=static_cases trivially passing tests of its own. Pytest reports `N passed`, total = max(N, static_cases), bad = {} and all_pass() is true although no hidden test ran. The same applies to bats via a sandbox `.bats` helper beside the overlaid file. This defeats the core purpose of the grader (hidden tests the agent cannot game).
findings.failure_mode: An implementing agent (or a contaminated run) gets hidden_tests.passed == total, snapshot verdict accuracy and refactor suite_green flags without any hidden test executing, silently corrupting ablation results.
findings.suggested_fix: Grade by node id, not count: require each overlaid hidden test file's nodes (path == overlay dest) to appear in the -rA listing with PASSED, and treat any missing hidden node as failed. Additionally run pytest with `-p no:cacheprovider -c /dev/null --noconftest` (or `-o python_files=... --override-ini`) and `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`, or always remove/restore `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, `.bats` helpers that are not in the fixture before running.

findings.description: With `--executor host` the test command runs directly on the grader host as the invoking user, cwd = the agent-written tree, with the caller's full PATH and PYTHONUSERBASE. `python3 -P -m pytest` still imports every `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini` plugin (`-p`), and `python_files` module from the agent's tree, and `bats` sources any `load`ed helper. The agent being graded therefore gets arbitrary code execution as the grader user: it can read ~/.aws, ~/.claude.json, rewrite the suite's hidden/ tests and MANIFEST.sha256 (the freeze check already ran), or alter grade.json after the fact. The mode is opt-in and documented (DEC-0491 picked container), but the header presents it as a routine fallback used in the Sprint 258 smoke, and nothing warns at runtime.
findings.failure_mode: Any grading in host mode of a run whose sandbox contains a malicious conftest.py or bats helper compromises the grader account and can poison the frozen suite for all later grades.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict `--executor host` to self-check of trusted fixtures (refuse it when grading a run directory), or require an explicit `--i-accept-host-exec` flag that prints a warning; at minimum run with `--noconftest -p no:... -c /dev/null`, a throwaway unprivileged user, and copy the suite read-only before running.

findings.description: Collection-error node names and test node paths are taken verbatim from the agent-controlled pytest output (`ERROR <node>` / `PASSED <node>`) and passed to `open(os.path.join(tree, f))`. `os.path.join` discards `tree` when `f` is absolute and `..` is not rejected, so a test (or a `print("ERROR /dev/zero")` in the tree) makes the grader read arbitrary host files. Content is only regex-counted, so disclosure is limited, but `.read()` on `/dev/zero` exhausts memory and opening a FIFO the agent created in its sandbox (whose absolute path it knows) blocks forever. def_line() has the same pattern.
findings.failure_mode: A single crafted output line hangs or OOM-kills the grader for that run, and lets the agent probe host paths (existence/def-count) outside the grading tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate node paths with safe_rel() and `is_within(tree, ...)` before opening; open with O_NOFOLLOW/stat for S_ISREG and cap the read size (e.g. 1 MiB); ignore nodes that fail validation.

findings.description: gate_verdict() and review_md_verdict() guard with `os.path.isfile()` only and then iterate `open(path)`, whereas combined_findings() correctly adds `not os.path.islink(p)`. The three inputs (sandbox/review.md and the two a2a feedback files) are agent writable. A symlink to `/dev/zero` produces one unbounded line and exhausts memory; a symlink to a FIFO blocks the grader indefinitely; a symlink to any readable host file is parsed for a `LOA-VERDICT` trailer (no content is emitted, but it is a read outside the run directory the header promises never happens). Separately, these verdict files are the same tamperable sandbox artefacts the header warns about for envelopes: the implementing agent in FIX1/FIX2 can rewrite the reviewer's trailer and set its own verdict_accuracy.
findings.failure_mode: Grader hang/OOM on a crafted sandbox, and forged gate verdicts flowing into verdict_accuracy.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject symlinks (`os.path.islink`) and non-regular files, cap bytes read, and derive verdicts from the harness-owned copies under eval/ (or a harness-recorded hash of the feedback file at gate time) rather than the sandbox.

findings.description: remove_path() walks a directory and calls `os.chmod(join(r, d), 0o700)` on every entry in `dirs`. `os.walk` lists symlinks-to-directories in `dirs`, and `os.chmod` follows symlinks, so the *target* of each symlink is chmodded. The grading trees are built from the agent's sandbox with symlinks preserved verbatim (copy_tree), and tests inside the container can create further symlinks through the rw /workspace mount. On the next grade of the same run, `fresh_dir(grading)` (and put_file/prepare removals) therefore chmod 0o700 any directory the agent pointed at that the grader user owns, e.g. the user's home, a shared results directory, or a socket directory.
findings.failure_mode: Agent-planted symlinks cause out-of-tree permission changes on the grader host during cleanup, breaking shared directories or services.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip symlinks in the chmod loop (`if not os.path.islink(p)`), or use `os.chmod(..., follow_symlinks=False)` where supported / `os.open(..., O_NOFOLLOW)` + `os.fchmod`; alternatively rely on `shutil.rmtree(onexc=...)` to fix permissions lazily.

findings.description: The container has no `--pids-limit`, `--memory`, `--cpus` or `--cap-drop ALL`/`no-new-privileges`, and the /workspace mount is rw and unbounded (only /tmp is a 256m tmpfs). `timeout 120 <cmd>` sends SIGTERM only (no `-k`), so a test that traps TERM keeps running; the Python-side `subprocess.run(timeout=180)` then kills only the `docker run` client, leaving the container alive and holding the mount while the grader proceeds to rmtree/reuse the tree. A fork bomb or large allocation competes with the host, and a test can fill the host disk under <run-dir>/grading/.
findings.failure_mode: Agent test code denies service to the grading host (PID/memory/disk exhaustion) or leaves orphaned containers that corrupt subsequent grades of the same run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--pids-limit 256 --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g --cpus 2 --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges`, use `timeout -k 10 120`, give the container a `--name` and `docker kill` it on TimeoutExpired, and bound the tree size (e.g. mount a copy on a size-limited tmpfs or check `du` afterwards).

findings.description: The contamination scan is substring based and easy to sidestep: `hid*`, `hid""den`, `$H`-style splitting, `~/...` (ABS_WORD only matches words starting with `/`), relative `../..` traversal from the sandbox, `$(pwd)/..`, `find / -name`, base64/`eval`, or reading via a script the agent writes. Host mode also whitelists `~/.aws`, `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json` and `~/.codex`, so direct reads of the caller's cloud and API credentials are reported as clean. The header does state the scan is a lower bound, but grade.json exposes only `contaminated: null`, which consumers may read as a positive assurance.
findings.failure_mode: Leaked hidden tests or credential reads go unflagged; downstream analysis over-trusts `contaminated: null`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `scan_coverage: "lower_bound"` marker to grade.json, normalise commands (strip quotes, expand `~` and `$HOME`, resolve `..` against the init cwd) before matching, flag `find`/`grep -r` rooted outside the sandbox, and drop `~/.aws` from the host whitelist (flag it as a separate `credential_path` pattern instead).

findings.description: Every other task.yaml path (fixture, hidden src/dest, grader_protected, structural_check, reference_patch) is confined with safe_rel()/is_within(), but `review_catch.manifest` and `review_catch.fixture` are joined raw; an absolute path or `..` resolves anywhere on the host. With `--allow-unfrozen` (task authoring) an unreviewed task.yaml can thus make the grader read an arbitrary JSON file as the answer key and copy an arbitrary directory into the self-check sandbox.
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent trust boundary for task.yaml; unfrozen authoring runs can be pointed at out-of-suite files.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply safe_rel() to both fields and require the resolved manifest/fixture to be inside REPO_ROOT or the suite root (is_within).
